headline.text: Kainuu's crude shares for overlapping treatment categories lag Finland in curative (20.8%, 95% CI 16.0–26.6 vs 27.0%) and life-prolonging care (18.6%, 95% CI 14.1–24.2 vs 30.4%).

details.text: Because a patient can receive several treatments, these treatment categories overlap: Kainuu's crude curative share of 20.8% (95% CI 16.0–26.6; n=47/226) and crude life-prolonging share of 18.6% (95% CI 14.1–24.2; n=42/226) have 95% confidence intervals that exclude the national values of 27.0% (4009/14873) and 30.4% (4522/14873).

Across these overlapping categories, Kainuu's crude symptomatic treatment share is 48.2% (95% CI 41.8–54.7; n=109/226), with a 95% confidence interval that excludes the national 39.5% (5871/14873), whereas the crude share with no treatment record within 12 months is 28.3% (95% CI 22.9–34.5; n=64/226), whose 95% confidence interval includes and is not distinguishable from the national 27.5% (4089/14873).

Kainuu's crude share of patients with a recorded MDT meeting is 0.9% (95% CI 0.2–3.2; n=2/226), with a 95% confidence interval excluding the national 6.0% (893/14873), though MDT records measure recording practice rather than care because HILMO captures codes WZC15 and WZC20 only from direct patient contacts.

Nationally, preliminary figures show lung cancer care takes 155 days on average from symptoms to treatment in Finland (56 days patient delay, 41 days in primary care, and 58 days in specialist care, the longest stage), compared with 107 days in Sweden and 67 days in Denmark, while public data lack county waiting times.

headline.text: Kainuu's treatment shares are crude—neither age-adjusted nor stage-adjusted—and public registry data do not capture primary care, referrals, or pathway waiting times.

details.text: Kainuu's county shares are crude and have separate limitations: they are not age-adjusted (age-adjusted values exist only from Kuva 16 for curative treatment by sex, digitised at ±0.5 percentage points precision, with national lines of 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women), and separately they cannot be stage-adjusted because stage at diagnosis is missing for about 48% of patients.

A journal article reports that HILMO diagnoses match the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types, which concerns diagnosis concordance only, while the 27.5% national and 28.3% (95% CI 22.9–34.5) crude Kainuu shares with no treatment record within 12 months mix untreated patients and unrecorded treatment.

Primary care visits are not included in the report's data, occupational health is not mentioned, symptom and referral dates are absent, imaging appears only indirectly as clinical-only diagnosis (about 20% of patients), and HILMO shows whether a specialist visit (93.6% nationally, up to 3 months before diagnosis) or treatment occurred within 12 months, not when.

headline.text: The team recommends that Kainuu report THL 21/2016 access times with handover alerts, adopt a KYS-style referral template and contact model, and publish how completely stage, drugs, and MDT are recorded.

details.text: The team recommends reporting lung cancer access times using THL guidance Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions (covering 16 cancers) and flagging stalled handovers, because the Health Care Act sets no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion and the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation with recommended time limits is to be carried out before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

The team recommends a KYS-style referral template, referring persistent symptoms after a normal X-ray, and a diagnostic-phase contact person: mentor insight notes weak referrals get lower urgency, reviewed regional pathway documents show only KYS has those referral rules and no reviewed region names a diagnostic contact, and STM roadmap measure 1.2.3 plans coordinator guidance by 2026–2028 (adopted 2029–2031) without specifying the phase.

Given Kainuu's crude 0.9% (95% CI 0.2–3.2; n=2/226) recorded MDT share versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, missing stage for about 48% of patients, and incomplete national data collection, the team recommends publishing per county how completely stage, drug treatment, and MDT meetings are recorded while STM roadmap measure 3.2.1 plans a quality registry (decree 2026–2028; reports 2029–2031 at 90% coverage).

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.
rec:1.location: §1. Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts

rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.
rec:2.location: §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact

rec:3.claim_text: Team recommendation 3: Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding. Publish, per county, how completely stage, drug treatment and MDT meetings are recorded. Read county ‘gaps’ in these fields as data-quality signals first.
rec:3.location: §3. Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding
